title: Grateful Dead Live at Golden Hall, Community Concourse on 1982-02-19
lineage: 6th row center:  Sony ECM 220T mics on hats > Sony TCDM5 Cassette tape on Sony FeCr Type III tapes with Dolby B OnPlayback by Rango Keshavan Nak DR1 EQ Type II, Dolby B On > Sony PCMR500 DAT deck SBM On > Monster Digital Coax Cab

ai_review.summary: Audience‑sourced recording with fair sound captures a high‑energy San Diego show highlighted by a monster Other One and the Lost Sailor suite.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its energetic jams – especially The Other One’s thunderous bass line, the Lost Sailor > Saint of Circumstance sequence and lively space work. Recording quality is mixed: many listeners enjoy the overall vibe, but several note thin mids, out‑of‑phase moments and monitor wash that dulls clarity.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~3.8; show is generally praised (high energy, standout songs) while recording receives mixed feedback, leading to a balanced 4‑star assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound described as wonderful by some but also thin on Dire Wolf, out of phase in parts, monitor wash and balance issues near the front of house; occasional vocal drop‑outs and P.A. lag.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set uneven with some lackluster moments; second set picks up strong energy, especially in The Other One and space jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is noted for lively solos (e.g., Cassidy) but suffers from occasional out‑of‑phase texture.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s thunderous bass line on The Other One is highlighted as a rare, powerful moment.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals are reported as thin or swallowed in spots (e.g., El Paso, Candyman).
